title: Docker Announces Hardened Images Catalog to Strengthen Enterprise Software Supply Chain Security
summary: PALO ALTO, Calif. – May 19, 2025 – Docker, Inc.®, a leading provider of cloud-native application development tools, content, and services for developers,
body_text: Press Release Docker Announces Hardened Images Catalog to Strengthen Enterprise Software Supply Chain Security New offering accelerates secure app delivery, giving platform and security teams enterprise-grade control without slowing developers down PALO ALTO, Calif. – May 19, 2025 – Docker, Inc.® , a leading provider of cloud-native application development tools, content, and services for developers, including emerging AI workflows, today announced Docker Hardened Images (DHI), a curated catalog of security-hardened, enterprise-grade container images designed to meet today’s toughest software supply chain challenges. Designed with security at the core, Docker Hardened Images are minimal, continuously maintained, and tested to meet enterprise compliance standards. Available directly through Docker Hub, DHI enables developers, security engineers, and platform teams to scale securely without disrupting familiar workflows. “The complexity of securing container dependencies shouldn’t fall squarely on developers’ shoulders,” said Michael Donovan, vice president of Product at Docker. “With Docker Hardened Images, we’re making it easier for teams to build with trusted and verified components that meet enterprise-grade security and compliance standards without adding friction to their workflow.” An Emerging Market, A Trusted Differentiator Docker is uniquely positioned to deliver this. With over a decade of experience building tools developers love and securing billions of image pulls every month on Docker Hub, Docker Hardened Images are a natural evolution of Docker’s platform, built directly into the workflows teams already trust. The result: a secure, flexible foundation that works out of the box and meets the needs of modern enterprise teams. At launch several partners are joining Docker to support the Docker Hardened Images ecosystem, including leading software publishers and security providers. These partners help deliver secure, enterprise-ready images and integrate enhanced scanning, metadata, and compliance insights into existing workflows. Their collaboration reflects the growing demand for trusted, scalable solutions that reduce container risk without slowing development. Partners announced today include Cloudsmith , GitLab , Grype , JFrog , Microsoft , Neo4j , NGINX , Sonatype , Sysdig , and Wiz , with more yet to come. “Docker’s Hardened Images are a major step forward in software supply chain assurance,” said Steven Dickens, CEO and Principal Analyst at HyperFRAME Research . “In a market still in its early stages, developers and enterprises are looking for a trusted partner who understands both scale and simplicity. Docker brings years of ecosystem leadership to the hardened container space, combining security, usability, and seamless integration in a way that few others can. ” “Wiz is excited to see Docker entering the container vulnerability management space with their Hardened Images offering,” said Oron Noah, Vice President of Product, Extensibility & Partnerships at Wiz. “Improving the software supply chain takes collaboration across the ecosystem. With Docker’s key position in the container ecosystem and the reach of Docker Hub, this initiative has the potential to dramatically improve software supply chain security across the industry.” Built for the Enterprise Developer Modern software teams move fast but security, compliance, and trust can’t be left behind. Docker Hardened Images are built for the real-world needs of enterprise developers and the teams that support them. Whether you’re responsible for building, securing, or scaling applications, DHI helps you move faster with guardrails in place: Platform Engineers gain a scalable way to manage secure, compliant images with full control over policies and provenance Application Developers can focus on shipping code, not chasing CVEs, with hardened, ready-to-run images integrated into Docker Hub Security Engineers get consistent, verifiable artifacts that align with organization-wide security standards and simplify audits CISOs gain supply chain visibility and assurance that container dependencies meet compliance expectations out of the box Secure by Default, Flexible by Design Docker Hardened Images are engineered to provide maximum security and compliance while staying lightweight, fast, and customizable. Each image is: Built to eliminate vulnerabilities , with few-to-zero exploitable CVEs and continuous scanning and updates, all built to meet SLSA Build Level 3 requirements Designed for least privilege , running as non-root by default to reduce risk in production Minimized by design , based on distroless principles that reduce attack surface and improve startup time, with up to 95% reduction in attack surface Compliance-ready: SBOMs, VEX, build provenance, and more — all cryptographically signed. Available across multiple distros —including Alpine and Debian—with more to come, supporting a wide range of enterprise environments. Now Available on Docker Hub Docker Hardened Images are now available on Docker Hub—discover how your team can get started . Resources Blog: Introducing Docker Hardened Images: Secure, Minimal, and Ready for Production Product: Docker Hardened Images About Docker Docker drives modern software development by making it easy to adopt container technology to radically boost productivity, security, testing, and collaboration at every step of the developer experience. Embraced by over 20 million developers worldwide, Docker’s unmatched flexibility and choice make it the preferred tool for developers seeking efficiency and innovation for creating modern applications. Learn more about Docker at www.docker.com . Contact David Oro press@docker.com

title: Guía SEO: Cómo crear una + Plantilla gratuita
summary: Un documento de hoja de ruta SEO describe los pasos para mejorar el rendimiento de búsqueda de su sitio web. Aprende cómo crear uno.
body_text: Hemos traducido este artículo del inglés al español. Haz clic aquí para leer el artículo original. Si detectas algún problema en el contenido, no dudes en escribirnos a report-osteam@semrush.com . ¿Qué es una hoja de ruta SEO? Una hoja de ruta SEO es un documento que formaliza un plan paso a paso para mejorar el rendimiento de su sitio web en los motores de búsqueda. Incluye tareas, plazos y responsables. Está adaptado a tus objetivos SEO únicos. Y trabajar para lograrlos debería, en última instancia, ayudarte a alcanzar tus objetivos empresariales generales. Puedes crear una hoja de ruta SEO utilizando una hoja de cálculo de Google o cualquier otra herramienta de gestión de proyectos. Aquí tenéis un ejemplo de cómo podría verse: Descarga nuestra plantilla gratuita de hoja de ruta SEO para seguir con el resto de esta guía. Por qué necesitas una hoja de ruta SEO Aquí tienes algunas maneras en que una hoja de ruta SEO te puede ayudar: Simplificar tareas complejas Una hoja de ruta SEO divide el proceso SEO en tareas más pequeñas y manejables. Por ejemplo, en lugar de tener como objetivo general "mejorar el SEO", la hoja de ruta podría comenzar con una investigación específica de palabras clave. Y luego pasar a optimizar las páginas individualmente. Priorizar los esfuerzos de alto impacto Utilizar una hoja de ruta te ayuda a centrarte en las acciones que generan los mayores beneficios. Así no pierdes el tiempo en cosas que no tendrán ningún impacto. Por ejemplo, si la mayor parte de su tráfico orgánico proviene de unas pocas páginas con un rendimiento superior, su hoja de ruta podría priorizar la optimización de ese contenido antes de crear nuevas páginas. Adaptarse a las actualizaciones de los motores de búsqueda Tu hoja de ruta es un documento vivo. Así que puedes ajustarlo en respuesta a los cambios en el algoritmo del motor de búsqueda . Para garantizar que sus esfuerzos de SEO sigan siendo efectivos a lo largo del tiempo. Por ejemplo, si Google comienza a priorizar las métricas de experiencia del usuario (UX) en el futuro, su hoja de ruta podría cambiar para priorizar la mejora de la navegación con menús fáciles de usar por encima de todo lo demás. Cómo crear y utilizar una hoja de ruta SEO Crear e implementar una hoja de ruta SEO implica mucha planificación preliminar y colaboración. Aquí te explicamos cómo hacerlo: 1. Define tus objetivos de SEO Tener objetivos de SEO claros te ayuda a concentrarte en las tácticas más impactantes (que cubriremos más en el paso ocho). Y te proporciona una forma clara de medir el éxito más adelante. Comience por identificar qué desea lograr con sus esfuerzos de SEO. Ya sea para aumentar el conocimiento de la marca, generar clientes potenciales o cualquier otra cosa. Luego, establezca objetivos específicos, medibles, alcanzables, relevantes y con plazos definidos (SMART) para garantizar que sus objetivos sean claros y prácticos. Digamos que su empresa quiere aumentar las ventas online un 10% durante el próximo año. Así pues, usted respalda eso estableciendo un objetivo de SEO para aumentar el tráfico orgánico en un 25% en los próximos nueve meses. ¿Cuál crees que es factible teniendo en cuenta tu presupuesto y las limitaciones de recursos? Su principal indicador clave de rendimiento (KPI) es el tráfico orgánico. Pero es posible que desee establecer algunos KPI de SEO más , como clasificaciones de palabras clave y tasa de clics (CTR). Luego, establezca plazos claros para garantizar que su equipo se mantenga en el buen camino y progrese constantemente hacia sus objetivos. Al definir los plazos para tus tareas, ten en cuenta estos consejos: Ten en cuenta la carga de trabajo y otros compromisos de los miembros del equipo para que tus estimaciones de tiempo sean realistas. Añade flexibilidad a tus plazos para adaptarte a imprevistos o retrasos. Revise y ajuste periódicamente sus plazos según sea necesario, en función del progreso, los cambios de prioridades o la nueva información. 2. Analiza tus KPI de SEO Analizar tu desempeño actual con los KPI que has establecido puede ayudarte a comprender cuánto necesitas mejorar para alcanzar tu objetivo. Digamos que tus KPIs son el posicionamiento de palabras clave y el tráfico orgánico. Deberás obtener mediciones de referencia para cada una de estas métricas. Y quizás alguna información complementaria. Utilice Google Analytics para realizar un seguimiento del tráfico orgánico. Inicie sesión en su cuenta de GA y vaya a la pestaña " Informes ". A continuación, haga clic en “ Adquisición ” > “ Adquisición de tráfico .” Podrás ver todo el tráfico del período seleccionado desglosado por canal. Asegúrese de tener en cuenta la fila de “Búsqueda orgánica”, ya que esta indica la cantidad de tráfico orgánico que recibe su sitio web. A continuación, utilice la herramienta de seguimiento de posición de Semrush para ver qué tan bien se está posicionando para sus palabras clave objetivo. Abre la herramienta y crea un proyecto si aún no lo has hecho. A continuación, introduce tu dominio y haz clic en " Configurar seguimiento ." Complete la configuración. (Siga esta guía de configuración si necesita ayuda.) Una vez finalizada la configuración, verá un informe de "Paisaje". Lo cual resume la visibilidad de tu dominio, el tráfico estimado y la posición promedio para tus palabras clave monitorizadas. Ve a la pestaña “ Resumen ” y desplázate hacia abajo hasta la sección “Resumen de clasificaciones”. Esta sección muestra la posición de su sitio web en los resultados de búsqueda para palabras clave individuales y cómo han cambiado esas posiciones con respecto al período anterior. Comprender el posicionamiento actual de tus palabras clave y el tráfico orgánico te ayudará a medir tu progreso a lo largo del camino. 3. Realizar una auditoría técnica . . Una buena experiencia de usuario (UX) es especialmente importante porque puede reducir la tasa de rebote y animar a los visitantes a explorar más páginas. Y ofrecer una experiencia de usuario positiva puede mejorar el rendimiento de tu estrategia SEO. . Encuentra estos problemas utilizando la herramienta Auditoría del sitio de Semrush. Abra la herramienta, introduzca su dominio y haga clic en " Iniciar auditoría ." Verás la opción "Configuración de auditoría del sitio". Completa la configuración para configurar tu primer rastreo del sitio web y haz clic en “ Iniciar auditoría del sitio .” (Siga esta guía de configuración si necesita ayuda.) Una vez finalizada la auditoría, verá un informe de "Resumen". Lo primero que debes observar es la puntuación de salud del sitio. Se calcula en función del número de errores y advertencias encontrados en su sitio web. Cuanto mayor sea este número, mejor. A continuación, vaya a la pestaña " Problemas " para ver la lista de problemas en su sitio. Verás "Errores", que son los más graves. Además de las “Advertencias”, también existen problemas de gravedad media. Y “Avisos”: cuestiones no críticas que conviene abordar. Para problemas individuales, haga clic en " Por qué y cómo solucionarlo " para obtener más información sobre el problema y cómo abordarlo. Toma nota de los problemas que se mencionan aquí para que puedas priorizar cuáles agregar a tu hoja de ruta. 4. Descubra oportunidades de optimización en la página El SEO en la página ayuda a los motores de búsqueda a comprender el contenido de sus páginas, aumentando las posibilidades de obtener una mejor posición en la SERP para las palabras clave relevantes. Algunos elementos clave de la página incluyen los títulos de página (también llamados H1), los encabezados, las meta descripciones (HTML que resume brevemente una página) y la estructura de la URL. Utilice el comprobador de SEO en página de Semrush para obtener ideas para mejorar el SEO en página de su sitio. Abre la herramienta, introduce tu dominio y haz clic en " Obtener ideas ." Complete la configuración. (Siga esta guía de configuración si necesita ayuda.) Una vez que la herramienta esté lista, verá un informe de "Resumen" como este: Vaya a la pestaña “ Ideas de optimización ”. Encontrarás ideas específicas para cada página relacionadas con estrategia, contenido, enlaces entrantes, semántica, experiencia del usuario, etc. Haz clic en “ # ideas ” junto a una de las páginas para ver las recomendaciones para mejorar su SEO en la página. Luego, podrá ver las ideas agrupadas en las categorías “Estrategia” y “Contenido”. Por ejemplo, la sección de contenido te indicará si necesitas incorporar tus palabras clave objetivo en el H1, el cuerpo de la página y otras áreas clave. Repasa las ideas. Más adelante añadirás las más importantes a tu hoja de ruta. La idea es que cada página sea relevante y valiosa para tu audiencia. Por lo tanto, es más probable que aparezca en los resultados de búsqueda. Lecturas adicionales : Lista de verificación de SEO On-Page: La lista completa de tareas para 2024 5. Revisa tu perfil de backlinks . Por lo tanto, es una buena idea saber en qué situación te encuentras actualmente. Analice su perfil de backlinks actual utilizando Backlinks . La herramienta te muestra el número de enlaces entrantes que apuntan a tu sitio web. Y otras perspectivas adicionales. Abra la herramienta, ingrese su dominio y haga clic en “ Analizar .” En el informe “Resumen”, puede ver su “Puntuación de autoridad”, que es una medida de la salud general de su sitio en una escala de 100. Y tu “Puntuación de Toxicidad General”, una evaluación de cuántos enlaces entrantes de baja calidad apuntan a tu sitio. Es una buena idea considerar ambas métricas conjuntamente. Si tu puntuación de autoridad es baja y tu puntuación de toxicidad es alta, eso indica que debes trabajar para obtener más enlaces de sitios relevantes y de alta calidad. A continuación, vaya a la pestaña " Backlinks " para obtener una vista detallada de los backlinks individuales. . Y elimínelos o renúncielos. Utilizando esta herramienta, también puedes comparar el perfil de backlinks de tu sitio con el de tus competidores. Añade los dominios de tus competidores y verás un informe comparativo. Si descubre que sus competidores tienen más backlinks de alta calidad procedentes de sitios web relevantes de su sector, podría considerar la posibilidad de contactar con esos sitios para obtener backlinks. Toma nota de los siguientes pasos apropiados para que puedas determinar cómo proceder cuando empieces a elaborar tu hoja de ruta de SEO. Lecturas adicionales : Cómo realizar una auditoría de backlinks (5 sencillos pasos) 6. Identificar nuevas oportunidades de contenido Identificar qué contenido funciona mejor proporciona información sobre lo que disfrutan tus visitantes. Así podrás replicar ese éxito en el futuro. Para revisar el contenido existente, inicia sesión en Google Analytics . Ir a “ Informes ” > " Participación " > " Páginas y pantallas ." Y desplázate hacia abajo para ver la lista de páginas con visualizaciones, usuarios, tiempo medio de interacción y otros datos. Analiza estos datos para comprender qué temas conectan con tu público. Por ejemplo, si observa que sus guías detalladas atraen sistemáticamente más tráfico e interacción que las entradas de blog más cortas, puede centrarse en crear contenido más completo en el futuro. Además, identifica las lagunas de contenido: temas centrados en palabras clave por las que tus competidores se posicionan, pero tú no. Utilice la herramienta Keyword Gap para identificar dichos temas. Abre la herramienta, introduce tu dominio y los dominios de tus competidores, y haz clic en " Comparar ." Verás una lista de palabras clave comunes para las que todos los sitios web se posicionan. Haz clic en “ Falta ” para ver las palabras clave por las que todos tus competidores se posicionan pero tú no. A continuación, haga clic en “ Débil ” para ver las palabras clave para las que su sitio se clasifica por debajo de sus competidores. Descubrir estas carencias de palabras clave te permite crear contenido sobre temas que satisfacen necesidades de audiencia no cubiertas. Ahora, anota todas las palabras clave que quieres usar como objetivo y todo el contenido que quieres crear. Así podrás incorporarlas a tu estrategia SEO. Lecturas adicionales : Cómo encontrar & Analizar las palabras clave de la competencia 7. Enumera todas tus tareas de SEO Ahora, elabore una lista completa de tareas de SEO basada en los conocimientos recopilados de su auditoría técnica, auditoría de SEO en la página, análisis de backlinks e investigación de palabras clave . Supongamos que tu lista se ve así: Optimiza los títulos de página, las meta descripciones y las etiquetas de encabezado. Mejorar la compatibilidad con dispositivos móviles Corrige enlaces rotos y errores de rastreo. Contenido duplicado de la dirección Simplifica la arquitectura de tu sitio web Mejora tu estructura de enlaces internos Optimizar imágenes Mejora la estructura de encabezados dentro del contenido Implementar marcado de esquema Evaluar palabras clave Finalizar la lista de palabras clave Planificar el calendario de contenido Crea contenido nuevo dirigido a palabras clave de alto valor. Actualizar el contenido existente para mejorar su relevancia y calidad. Crea backlinks de alta calidad desde sitios web con autoridad. Rastrea las menciones sin enlace para convertirlas en enlaces entrantes. . 8. Identificar áreas prioritarias de acción Priorizar tus tareas de SEO te ayuda a crear un plan de acción enfocado que maximiza tus resultados y mantiene a tu equipo alineado con los objetivos más críticos. Lo que significa que no todas las tareas llegarán a tu hoja de ruta final. ¿Cómo puedes priorizar tus tareas? Aquí hay algunos factores a considerar: Alineación con tus objetivos de SEO impacto potencial Esfuerzo requerido para la implementación Dependencia de otras tareas o recursos Un método eficaz consiste en utilizar una matriz de prioridades, donde se representa cada tarea en función de su impacto y esfuerzo. Las tareas que se encuentran en el cuadrante de "Victorias rápidas" (alto impacto y bajo esfuerzo) deben abordarse primero. Porque ofrecen los beneficios más significativos con la menor inversión. Los elementos del cuadrante "Grandes Apuestas" (alto impacto, alto esfuerzo) deben planificarse y ejecutarse cuidadosamente. Las "tareas de relleno" (de bajo impacto y poco esfuerzo) pueden utilizarse para completar los huecos en su documento de hoja de ruta SEO si dispone de espacio para ellas. Las "tareas ingratas" (de bajo impacto y alto esfuerzo) deberían omitirse o reevaluarse más adelante. Por ejemplo, actualizar las etiquetas de título de las páginas clave podría ser una "victoria rápida", mientras que una reestructuración de la arquitectura del sitio podría ser una "gran apuesta". Ahora que ha refinado su lista para centrarse en las tareas más importantes, agréguelas a su copia de la plantilla de hoja de ruta de SEO . 9. Establecer hitos para el seguimiento del progreso Los hitos son puntos de control importantes en tu recorrido de SEO que resaltan el progreso hacia tus objetivos. Te ofrecen una visión general de tu progreso global. Por ejemplo, sus hitos podrían incluir: Completar las mejoras técnicas de SEO para finales del primer trimestre Publicar 10 nuevas entradas de blog con palabras clave específicas para finales del segundo trimestre. Actualizar todo el contenido con mejor rendimiento para finales del tercer trimestre. Y recuerda comprobar periódicamente cómo estás progresando. Recomendamos hacerlo cada mes y anotarlo en la columna correspondiente de su hoja de cálculo. 10. Asignar recursos Una asignación eficaz de recursos garantiza que dispongas de las habilidades y herramientas necesarias para ejecutar tu plan. Comience por evaluar los recursos necesarios para cada tarea en su lista de prioridades. Esto puede incluir: Tiempo del personal interno (por ejemplo, creadores de contenido, desarrolladores y especialistas en SEO) Experiencia externa (por ejemplo, profesionales independientes, agencias y consultores) Herramientas (por ejemplo, herramientas SEO, herramientas de análisis y un sistema de gestión de contenidos) En función de esta evaluación, asigne primero sus recursos disponibles a las tareas de mayor prioridad. Sé realista sobre lo que puedes lograr con tus recursos actuales y considera si son necesarias inversiones adicionales para alcanzar tus objetivos (y dentro de tu presupuesto). Finalmente, asigne miembros específicos del equipo o socios externos para que sean responsables de ejecutar e informar sobre cada elemento. Y anótalo en tu hoja de cálculo. Esto garantiza que todos conozcan su función y contribuyan al éxito general de su estrategia SEO. 11. Colaborar con las partes interesadas La comunicación con las partes interesadas es clave para obtener su apoyo a tu estrategia de SEO. Y demostrando su éxito más adelante. Comience por presentar su hoja de ruta a las partes interesadas clave. Recoge sus comentarios y aclara cualquier duda que puedan tener. Lo más importante es estar dispuesto a adaptar la hoja de ruta según sea necesario. Las prioridades empresariales pueden cambiar, y las aportaciones de las partes interesadas pueden aportar perspectivas valiosas. Una vez que haya comenzado a implementar la hoja de ruta, comunique regularmente el progreso de sus esfuerzos de SEO a las partes interesadas. Y comparte cómo vas avanzando hacia tus KPIs. 12. Evalúa los resultados y revisa tu hoja de ruta. El SEO es un proceso continuo, no un proyecto puntual. Por lo tanto, tu hoja de ruta SEO debe ser un documento vivo que evolucione a medida que progresas y aprendes. Normalmente, una hoja de ruta para SEO tiene una duración de seis a doce meses. Una vez completadas todas las tareas de la hoja de ruta inicial, es hora de evaluar los KPI para comprobar si se han alcanzado los objetivos. Si lo hiciste, crea una nueva hoja de ruta que se base en tu progreso y aborde los aspectos que no pudiste cubrir en la primera. Por ejemplo, si tu primera hoja de ruta se centró principalmente en la investigación de palabras clave y las optimizaciones técnicas, tu siguiente hoja de ruta podría priorizar la creación de contenido en torno a esas palabras clave y la generación de backlinks de alta calidad. Si no has alcanzado tus objetivos, es posible que necesites crear una hoja de ruta que aborde nuevos desafíos. O quizás necesites ajustar tus objetivos. Lecturas adicionales : Resultados SEO: Cómo realizar un seguimiento & Medir el rendimiento SEO Construye una base sólida con una hoja de ruta SEO Una hoja de ruta SEO eficaz utiliza datos para definir pasos y tareas exactas. Utilice las herramientas adecuadas para obtener estos datos. Comienza por auditar tu sitio web y comprender mejor sus fortalezas y debilidades en cuanto a SEO. Regístrate gratis en Semrush para comenzar con la auditoría del sitio .

summary: Total revenue in the year of $1,076.8 million, an increase of 18% year-over-year Total revenue in the quarter of $253.4 million, grew 10% year-over-year Gross margin improved to 44%, with gross profit increasing […]
body_text: Find news All Product Company Data and Insights Company Lightspeed Announces Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Financial Results and Provides Outlook for Fiscal 2026 2025-05-22 minute read Share Total revenue in the year of $1,076 .8 million, an increase of 18% year-over-year Total revenue in the quarter of $253 .4 million, grew 10% year-over-year Gross margin improved to 44%, with gross profit increasing 12% year-over-year Monthly ARPU1 grew 13% year-over-year to ~$489 while subscription ARPU 1 grew 11% Repurchased ~18.7 million shares, or ~12% of total shares outstanding, for proceeds of ~$219 million in last 12 months2 Lightspeed reports in US dollars and in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards. MONTREAL , May 22, 2025 – Lightspeed Commerce Inc., the one-stop commerce platform empowering merchants to provide the best omnichannel experiences, today announced financial results for the three months and fiscal year ended March 31, 2025 . “Fiscal 2025 was a transformative year for Lightspeed: we delivered revenue growth of 18% with annual revenue exceeding $1 billion for the first time, we adopted a more focused strategy, concentrating on the markets where we have a proven right to win, and we aligned our organization to execute on that strategy,” said Dax Dasilva , Founder and CEO. “With a strong financial foundation and our industry-leading commerce platforms, Fiscal 2026 will be dedicated to growing locations, expanding software revenue and enhancing Adjusted EBITDA profitability.” “Our healthy balance sheet, improving Adjusted EBITDA profitability and free cash flow nearing break-even enabled us to return ~$219 million of capital to shareholders in the last year,” said Asha Bakshani , CFO. “At the same time, we strategically invested in product and go-to-market for retail customers in North America and hospitality customers in Europe , laying the groundwork for continued success.” Fourth Quarter Financial Highlights (All comparisons are relative to the three-month period ended March 31, 2024 unless otherwise stated): Total revenue of $253.4 million , an increase of 10% year-over-year. Transaction-based revenue of $157.8 million , an increase of 14% year-over-year. Subscription revenue of $87.9 million , an increase of 8% year-over-year. Net loss of ($575.9) million , or ($3.79) per share, as compared to a net loss of ($32.5) million , or ($0.21) per share. Net loss includes a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of ($556.4) million . After adjusting for certain items, such as goodwill impairment and share-based compensation, the Company delivered an Adjusted Income3 of $15.0 million , or $0.10 per share3, as compared to Adjusted Income3 of $8 .5 million, or $0.06 per share3. Adjusted EBITDA3 of $12 .9 million versus Adjusted EBITDA3 of $4 .4 million. Cash flows used in operating activities of ($9.9) million as compared to cash flows used in operating activities of ($28.5) million , and Adjusted Free Cash Flow3 used of ( $9.3 ) million as compared to Adjusted Free Cash Flow3 used of ( $16.3 ) million. As at March 31, 2025 , Lightspeed had $558.5 million in cash and cash equivalents. Full Fiscal Year Financial Highlights (All comparisons are relative to the full fiscal year ended March 31, 2024 unless otherwise stated): Total revenue of $1,076.8 million , an increase of 18% year-over-year. Transaction-based revenue of $697.3 million , an increase of 28% year-over-year. Subscription revenue of $344.8 million , an increase of 7% year-over-year. Net Loss of ($667.2) million , or ($4.34) per share, as compared to a net loss of ($164.0) million , or ($1.07) per share. Net loss includes a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of ($556.4) million . After adjusting for certain items such as goodwill impairment and share-based compensation, the Company delivered an Adjusted Income3 of $69 .5 million, or $0.45 per share3 as compared to an Adjusted Income3 of $24 .5 million, or $0.16 per share3 in 2024. Adjusted EBITDA3 of $53 .7 million versus Adjusted EBITDA3 of $1 .3 million in 2024. Cash flows used in operating activities of ( $32.8 million ) as compared to cash flows used in operating activities of ( $97.7 million ), and Adjusted Free Cash Flow3 used of ( $11.2 ) million as compared to Adjusted Free Cash Flow3 used of ( $64.5 ) million in 2024. Fourth Quarter Operational Highlights Lightspeed delivered several new product releases in the quarter including: Seasonal trends and sales visualisations as part of Retail Insights, allowing merchants to forecast inventory with precision and interpret their data in visual formats; Generative AI web builder , enabling retailers to generate websites from simple screenshots with no manual coding required; Lightspeed NuORDER now includes PO Sync, a two-way sync to drive faster, automated replenishments for retailers and also now offers to connect multiple buyer accounts so that orders across different buying accounts seamlessly sync to the POS; Omni gift cards were upgraded to allow retailers to sell and redeem gift cards across in-store and online selling channels; Enhancements to Kitchen Display System, including advanced production instructions, which let servers add custom production instructions and allergen highlights to items, as well as consolidated item lists, which enable chefs in the kitchen to prepare items in batches when ordered from multiple tables. ARPU1,4 increased to ~$489 from ~$431 in the same quarter last year representing an increase of 13% driven by our focus on our unified POS and payments offering and growing subscription ARPU1 that increased 11%. Gross profit of $111.8 million increased 12% year over year. Overall gross margin was 44%, compared to 43% in the same quarter last year. Subscription gross margin grew to 81% in the quarter from 77% in the same quarter last year driven by a dedicated effort at controlling costs and targeted price increases. Transaction-based gross margin was 29% compared to 29% last year. Total GTV4 was $20 .6 billion. An increasing portion of GTV is being processed through the Company’s payments solutions. GPV4 increased 19% to $7 .9 billion in the quarter from $6 .6 billion in the same period last year, largely due to the Company’s unified POS and payments initiative. Customer Locations with GTV exceeding $500,000 /year5 and $1 million /year5 were flat and grew 2% year-over-year, respectively. Going forward, we are updating the definition of what constitutes a Customer Location. We have historically emphasized that a single unique customer can have multiple Customer Locations including physical and eCommerce sites, so eCommerce sites used by customers alongside a physical site have been counted as separate Customer Locations from the POS. As our POS and eCommerce solutions are packaged as a single omnichannel product, we believe this distinction has become less meaningful. Going forward, we will consider this product to be a single Customer Location. The end result is that the total number of Customer Locations4 changes from ~162,000 to ~144,000 as at March 31, 2025 while the monthly ARPU moves from ~$489 to ~$545 . All Customer Location growth targets provided at the Company’s Capital Markets Day on March 26, 2025 were aligned with this new definition. For additional details, please refer to the Customer Locations Reconciliation table at the end of this press release. Lightspeed Capital showed strong growth with revenue increasing 28% year-over-year. Notable customer wins for retail customers in North America : Runners Roost, Tennis Plaza, and WOODstack, retailers with advanced inventory requirements and multiple locations, selected Lightspeed Retail. In our Supplier Network we added several new brands, including Birkenstock Australia , Crew Clothing, and Tea Collection. In golf, we signed California’s Half Moon Bay Golf Links , host to two world class championship courses. Notable customer wins for hospitality customers in Europe : Lightspeed continued its winning streak with Michelin starred restaurants and chefs, signing La Vie in Dusseldorf , Zet’joe in Bruges, and Joelia in Rotterdam . In addition, the Company added the 18 locations of Burger & Sauce in the UK and luxury hotel Le Relais de Chambord in France . Given the recent volatility in the valuations of technology companies broadly and Lightspeed’s share price, the carrying amount of the Company’s net assets exceeded its market capitalization as at March 31, 2025 which triggered an impairment test to be performed for the Company. The goodwill impairment test resulted in a non-cash impairment charge of ( $556.4 ) million. Lightspeed hosted its Capital Markets Day on March 26, 2025 , where the Company outlined its three-year strategy and transformation journey. Lightspeed completed a share repurchase program that saw the Company repurchase a total of ~9.7 million shares for ~$134.2 million during the course of Fiscal 2025. Subsequent to the quarter, the Company completed its latest share repurchase program, repurchasing ~9.0 million shares for ~$84.4 million . Collectively, over the last twelve months, Lightspeed has spent ~$219 million to acquire ~18.7 million shares, representing ~12% of the total shares outstanding as at April 1, 2024 . The Company appointed Manon Brouillette to the role of Executive Chair and Dale Murray to the role of Lead Independent Director of its Board of Directors, in each case effective April 1, 2025 , to coincide with the start of the Company’s fiscal year. Financial Outlook6 The following outlook supersedes all prior statements made by the Company and is based on current expectations. As announced at its Capital Markets Day in March, Lightspeed expects to grow its outbound sales team to over 150 outbound sales representatives by the end of Fiscal 2026 in addition to increasing its investment in product and technology development by over 35%7. The benefits of these investments will likely be reflected in the latter half of the year as the new sales representatives ramp through the year. Lightspeed remains confident in its ability to execute its strategy of focusing on retail customers in North America and hospitality customers in Europe and expects to increase Customer Locations within these growth engines. With its increased investment in product and technology development, Lightspeed also expects to increase software revenue. Finally, the financial outlook reflects our most recent view of the macroeconomic environment and is consistent with our three-year target gross profit CAGR8 of approximately 15-18% and three-year target Adjusted EBITDA3 CAGR8 of approximately 35% presented at our Capital Markets Day in March. Overall, the Company’s outlook is as follows: First Quarter 2026 Revenue of approximately $285 million to $290 million . Gross profit growth of approximately 13%. Adjusted EBITDA3 of approximately $14 million to $16 million . Fiscal 2026 Revenue growth of approximately 10% to 12%. Gross profit growth of approximately 14%. Adjusted EBITDA3 of approximately $68 million to $72 million . title: The shifting supply landscape: 5 questions to ask your SSPs
summary: Agencies are rethinking SSP partnerships in favor of transparent, performance-driven supply paths. Here's why.
body_text: Table of contents What’s happening? Agencies are rethinking: From bundled control to transparent choice 5 questions to ask your SSPs right now Supply-side innovation Programmatic is changing. Again. This time, it’s a tectonic shift that many saw coming, but few were prepared to act on. Regulators have finally put vertically integrated ad tech stacks under the microscope, and the supply chain is rapidly adapting. For agencies and advertisers alike, that means hope for something better. A landmark ruling by a U.S. federal judge has made one thing clear: The future of digital advertising must be b uilt on bidding neutrality. The court found that Google’s control over both the sell side (AdX, GAM) and buy side (DV360, Google Ads) gave Google home‑field advantage. It ran the auction, placed its own bids, and kept everyone else in the dark. This ruling effectively breaks down the walled gardens and reopens the field for the rest of us. But agencies aren’t rushing to plug in more SSPs just for the sake of it. Instead, they’re looking to partner with SSPs who bring more to the auction than access alone, and who help create supply paths that are fairer, smarter, and more aligned with performance goals. What’s happening? For the first time in over a decade, we’re seeing a serious push toward neutral auctions, interoperable infrastructure, and transparent supply paths. A nd that’s creating a new mandate for agencies and advertisers to rethink how they prioritize SSPs and evaluate their media supply partners. Now, imagine every SSP bidding into the header auction at the exact same level. Even if this doesn’t flip market share overnight, the ripple effect could be huge – more competitive auctions, more diverse SSP wins, and, crucially, more value flowing back to publishers and advertisers. So, will this rebalance programmatic’s economy? Absolutely – and here’s why. Agencies are rethinking: From bundled control to transparent choice The recent ruling may reopen the field, but agencies aren’t simply adding more SSPs. They’re adding better ones. The old reliance on bundled ad tech stacks brought simplicity at the expense of transparency, leverage, and control. Today, with performance, accountability, and supply path optimization (SPO) at the top of every agenda , the long-held belief that “you can’t go wrong with Google” is starting to crack. Agencies are rewriting the playbook. Rather than treating consolidation as a virtue, they’re prioritizing strategic diversification to deliver more working media dollars and reduce single‑partner dependency. But we’re not going back to “plug everyone in and see what happens”. Agencies are becoming choosier – favoring SSPs that offer genuine differentiation , from commerce insights and advanced curation to transparent economics and stronger auction dynamics. As part of that shift, they’re asking whether existing supply paths still represent the highest quality, or whether new partners align better with their clients’ performance goals. Against this backdrop, agencies face a choice: Spread spend across more pipes or enhance supply through intelligence and intent. Increasingly, they’re choosing the latter, leveraging their own insights and first-party data to curate high-performing supply paths that reflect their unique value and deepen client trust. 5 questions to ask your SSPs right now As auction dynamics shift and competition hots up, now’s the time to audit your SSP relationships. Ask these five questions to ensure you’re partnering for value – not just scale. What differentiation do you offer beyond basic access? Is your SSP just a conduit to inventory, or does it offer something more – like unique commerce signals, curation tools, or operational efficiencies? Ask how they’re moving past legacy plumbing to create real value in a competitive, performance‑driven market. How transparent are your auctions and publisher practices? In an era of MFA concerns and opaque fee structures, transparency is non-negotiable. Understand how your SSP manages auctions, keeps them fair, and protects brand safety while providing efficient access to premium inventory. Can you drive commerce outcomes, not just deliver impressions? Performance media demands more than scale alone. Does your SSP help connect the dots between onsite and offsite signals – SKU-level intent, add-to-cart events, purchase verification – so you can tie spend to sales? How do you support first-party data activation and clean room integrations? Future-ready SSPs must enable secure, seamless collaboration across audience data ecosystems. Can your partner handle clean room workflows, curated deal creation, and first-party activation without adding friction? Are they lettingbuyers apply their own intelligence to the bid stream? How are you evolving with the market? Innovation should be proactive, not reactive. Whether through new formats, advanced packaging strategies, or deeper alignment between retail media and the open web, your SSP should be building for where the industry is heading – not where it’s been. Supply-side innovation The latest evolution of programmatic calls for supply partners that go beyond scale and focus on relevance, transparency, and measurable outcomes. Criteo Commerce Grid was built for that – offering tools and data that help agencies and brands connect with high-intent shoppers through smarter supply strategies. This is one of the many reasons why Criteo has recently been ranked as a high performer on Frost & Sullivan’s Innovation Index, within The Frost Radar ™, which reports on key features of the top 10 global leading SSPs. As agencies re-evaluate legacy partnerships and prioritize performance-driven supply paths, don’t just rebalance – upgrade . To learn more about how to activate, please reach out to your Criteo account manager, or talk to one of our experts.

title: The Future of MCP is GraphQL
body_text: Today we’re introducing Apollo MCP Server, enabling AI systems like Claude and GPT to interact with your organization’s APIs through GraphQL. While you can learn more about how to get started here, I wanted to share why we think GraphQL enabled by Model Context Protocol (MCP) will be an essential part of a modern AI stack. Connecting AIs to APIs MCP – a new protocol that standardizes how LLMs interface with external systems – opens the door wide open to agentic applications. APIs are the entry point to capabilities: adding items to carts, checking order status, scheduling appointments, updating inventory. When AI can reliably interact with these systems, we unlock an entirely more capable kind of software where natural language becomes the interface to complex business operations. MCP makes this possible by providing the connective tissue between AI’s language understanding and your API infrastructure. One approach to MCP is to build an MCP server for each API you want AI to access. Your payment API gets its own MCP server, your inventory system gets another, customer data gets a third. It’s a straightforward way to get started. Most teams can build an initial MCP for a service reasonably quickly and LLMs support multiple MCP tools. It makes for a compelling experience. As we’ve worked with teams pushing from prototype to product, we’re discovering that complex AI systems need more than what is possible by directly connecting individual APIs through MCP. We’ve found four particular requirements that show up consistently: Deterministic execution : An AI will often have to call multiple APIs in sequence and filter the results to just the appropriate fields for the user. This execution pattern needs to work exactly the same way every time for consistent, correct user experiences. Consider an AI returning purchase history – you can’t have one customer seeing five past orders while another sees three, or some results including shipping details while others don’t. We’ve also found that the more focused you keep the AI’s context, the better results you get. When APIs return large objects with hundreds of fields, the extra data can lead AI down unintended paths. Limiting data to exactly what’s needed keeps the AI on track and improves overall response quality. Policy enforcement : Giving AI direct access to individual APIs makes it difficult to enforce appropriate limits and access controls. A rule like “only loyalty members have access to the detailed shipping tracking information for their outstanding orders” can’t easily be written in the API layer, as it relates to a specific combination of data spread across multiple systems. Efficiency : Even simple customer queries can generate thousands of tokens when APIs return complete objects. Processing all of this and directly orchestrating multiple tool invocations from the AI becomes costly, both in terms of tokens and milliseconds. Agility : The pace of AI is unprecedented. The technology and techniques are progressing furiously. Just as interesting to me is that the freeform nature of AI makes it possible to deliver new functionality faster than ever before: most users wouldn’t tolerate a mobile app that changed every day, but continuous improvement of an AI agent is nothing but good news. So an AI stack needs to accommodate and facilitate a tempo we’ve never seen before in software development. This requirement rules out strategies that aren’t aligned to the modern platform engineering discipline of self-service tools and workflows. GraphQL solves these needs well What these requirements point to is the need for an abstraction layer between the AI and APIs. This orchestration layer exposes a set of MCP tools, where each tool provides a specific capability backed by some number of orchestrated API calls. The AI’s job is to reason about which MCP tools to invoke; the orchestration layer’s job is deterministic, efficient execution and policy enforcement. GraphQL is an ideal foundation of this orchestration layer. It’s declarative: MCP tools are defined in terms of schema and queries, rather than code. It’s performant: one GraphQL query can traverse your entire graph, gathering exactly what’s needed (and nothing that’s not) in an optimized way. It’s self-documenting: LLMs can reason about the meaning of the graph and its objects. It’s standards-based: a mature ecosystem with proven scalability. It’s self-service: on a GraphQL-based platform like Apollo, everyone with access to the graph can wire up MCP tools with the appropriate level of governance. The characteristics of GraphQL align perfectly with what AI needs to access APIs: a clean, understandable interface to AI while handling the messy reality of existing systems and services. Consider the earlier example of retrieving purchase history with shipping updates. A GraphQL query defines an MCP tool that the AI system can use. Under the hood, that query orchestrates multiple API calls into the order, shipping and loyalty systems and enforces the necessary policy check. That query can be authored and deployed by anyone on the platform, with the support of design and governance tools provided by the graph platform. The challenges an abstraction layer solves may seem like tomorrow’s problems when just getting started with MCP. It’s always worth planning for success, but a good declarative architecture also saves time and effort in the earliest stages of development. A GraphQL-based approach avoids having to build, debug and deploy custom MCP servers. Apollo Connectors let you bring REST APIs to GraphQL (and now MCP) without any modification. And the benefits of having a semantic API layer are truly remarkable – watching an LLM traverse a large GraphQL schema as it builds a new query is an exciting, eye-opening moment. Introducing Apollo MCP Server The Apollo MCP Server represents our continued investment in making GraphQL the best way to build modern API infrastructure. We’ve spent years developing tools that help teams build, manage, and scale GraphQL – from Apollo Client to Apollo Federation to our most recent innovation, Apollo Connectors . Now we’re extending that toolkit to address AI integration. By implementing MCP for GraphQL, we’re making it simple to connect AI to your existing graph. If you’re already using Apollo, this fits naturally into your stack. If you’re new to GraphQL, the MCP server provides a compelling entry point that solves immediate AI challenges while setting you up for future growth, all on top of the APIs you already have. We believe the architectural patterns emerging around AI – the need for precision, policy, efficiency, and agility – align perfectly with what GraphQL was designed to do. This MCP server is our way of helping teams realize those benefits. As you explore connecting AI to your services, consider not just immediate integration but your longer-term strategy. The architectural decisions you make today will determine how quickly and safely you can evolve AI capabilities tomorrow. Ready to get started? Connect your REST and GraphQL APIs to the Apollo MCP server today, explore our Odyssey training course, or join us at our upcoming event to learn more. The future of APIs is here – powered by graph-based API orchestration that makes it easier than ever to build applications. ​​ Written by Matt DeBergalis Read more by Matt DeBergalis

title: When to Use ChatGPT—and When to Use Product-Integrated AI
summary: Learn when to use flexible AI tools like ChatGPT vs product-integrated AI like Campfire, helping finance teams navigate where each fits best—based on the task, the risk, and the workflow
body_text: Blog Article Back to Home 2025-05-21 When to Use ChatGPT—and When to Use Product-Integrated AI Campfire Team May 21, 2025 General Accounting Finance ChatGPT is an incredible tool. Like any platform, it has its strengths and limitations—and knowing when to use it vs consider product-integrated AI is key to building an efficient, modern finance workflow. There’s never been a better time to explore AI in finance. The tools are powerful, the use cases are expanding, and the upside is huge. But not all AI is created equal. Some tools are designed for flexibility and brainstorming. Others are purpose-built for structured workflows. Understanding the difference can help you get the most out of both. What AI Is Actually Good At Right Now But before we get into when to use what, let’s take a moment to ground ourselves in what AI can actually do today. The hype is loud, but underneath it, the progress is real. AI is already strong at handling structured, rule-based tasks—especially when there’s clear context. That includes: Coding transactions Surfacing anomalies Drafting word-based responses (e.g. policies, memos, commentary) Reviewing human work for consistency Where it still struggles: Complex judgment or interpretation Tasks requiring deep business context and consistency Full autonomy in sensitive workflows (e.g. audit signoff, policy enforcement) That’s where understanding how to work best with AI, and keeping a human in the loop is important—and where choosing the right type of AI matters just as much. ChatGPT vs. Product-Integrated AI: What’s the Difference? 🧠 ChatGPT, Claude, and similar tools are flexible, open-ended interfaces that excel at: One-off projects Brainstorming ideas Writing first drafts Quick, unstructured research They shine when you need a fast starting point or a creative jumpstart. But they rely on you to provide context and ensure quality, making them less suited for high-volume, high-risk workflows. ⚙️ Product-Integrated AI (like Campfire) integrates AI directly into your financial systems. It understands your up to date data, structure, and policies—because it’s operating within them. At Campfire, we operate as a modern general ledger for mid-market finance & accounting teams—embedding AI & automation directly into your workflows so you can close fast, and scale faster. With Campfire’s product-integrated AI, you can: Audit the close by uploading your ASC 606 policy and having AI flag out-of-policy transactions Generate flux commentary with context-aware narrative tied to your actuals and budgets Draft complex, customized reports with a single prompt—no VLOOKUPs required Identify budget variances instantly and get AI-powered commentary Enforce policies by comparing memos to real-world entries (like prepaids or revenue schedules) In other words: this is AI that’s ready to run your process—not just assist with it. The Framework: When to Use What Here’s a simple way to think about it: Both tools have value. The key is knowing where each fits. Why It Matters You wouldn’t reconcile cash in a text editor. And you wouldn’t run your board reporting process in a Slack thread. ChatGPT can be a powerful partner in ideation, policy writing, and ad hoc analysis. But when the workflow repeats, the data matters, and collaboration or compliance is on the line—that’s where product-integrated AI like Campfire shines. Campfire’s AI doesn’t just generate responses. It understands your business context, operates with audit trails, and helps your team scale without adding headcount. TL;DR Use ChatGPT for one-off tasks, brainstorming, and drafts. Use product-integrated AI like Campfire for workflows that are structured, sensitive, or repeatable. The best finance teams use both—strategically. ChatGPT is a great place to start—whether you’re drafting a policy, exploring a new idea, or building a one-off analysis. But when you’re ready to execute those ideas at scale, tools like Campfire can help bring structure, context, and efficiency to your workflows. Ready to Get Started? title: How I Read 2000 Chinese Words in 30 Days Without Memorizing Flashcards

body_text: 1. I Thought This Was Impossible For years, I told myself I just wasn't good at reading Chinese. I could understand a few words when people spoke. I’d grown up hearing it at home — but when it came to actually reading signs, subtitles, or messages in Chinese? I was completely lost. I tried flashcards. I tried Duolingo. I even tried drilling HSK word lists. But nothing stuck. Every time I came back, it felt like starting over. 2. I Needed Something Different The turning point? A trip to Hong Kong. I was surrounded by menus and signs I couldn’t read — even though I knew some of the filler words, I didn't know any of the meaningful nouns. I realized: I wasn’t failing because I couldn’t learn. I was failing because I was going about learning the wrong way. I didn't have a consistent, and immersive way to learn for my level. These random one off spurts of motivation weren't enough to sustain real learning results. 3. I Found a New Way to Learn — And It Clicked That’s when I found Read Bean — a Chinese learning app that could actually support my level that was focused on real content and useful questions . I wasn’t sure at first, but after my first 5-minute reading lesson, I felt something shift. Instead of drilling random characters, I was: Reading about trending Chinese memes Learning words in real context Getting personalized quiz questions that felt like actual practice, not busywork 4. Exactly What I Did for 30 Days Day 1–3: Took the in-app level test Chose 3 starter lessons (mine were about Sun Wukong, some Chinese internet slang, and family terms) Day 4–10: Built a habit: every night before bed, I’d do 1 lesson Let the app track new words I saw and highlight ones I didn’t know Week 2–3: Started seeing repeated vocabulary naturally Focused more on sentence structure and context Paid attention to word usage through AI-generated questions Week 4: Cracked 2,000+ read words in the app Could read through short articles without translation Even wrote a few messages to a family member in Chinese — and they understood it. And understand a few Chinese spammer messages 5. What I Can Do Now vs 30 Days Ago Then: Could recognize 10–20 common characters Needed pinyin or translation constantly Now: Can read a short graded Chinese article without help Recognize patterns in grammar and slang Actually enjoy opening the app every day 6. Why It Worked This method works because: I was learning through real content with real context , not fake textbook examples The app adjusted to my level, showing me just-right material Vocabulary was learned in context , making it easier to remember It was fun . That meant I stuck with it. 7. If I Can Do This, So Can You You don’t need to move to China. You don’t need to spend $80/hour on a tutor. And you definitely don’t need to grind flashcards every night. You just need a system that works. Try Read Bean . It’s free to start, personalized to you, and it might change the way you learn Chinese — just like it did for me.

Device Engineering: Where Ambitions and Real Silicon Collide
summary: Behind the Builders: As the RibbonFET transistor arrives with Intel 18A, Chung-Hsun Lin works at the crossroads between silicon ambitions and physical reality.
body_text: Behind the Builders: As the RibbonFET transistor arrives with Intel 18A, Chung-Hsun Lin works at the crossroads of silicon ambitions and physical reality. In this article: When Global Foundries decided to shift away from the pursuit of leading-edge silicon technology nodes in 2018 (after IBM did in 2015), Chung-Hsun Lin wasn’t ready to give up. “At that time, I found in my heart, I still want to get my hands dirty working on the leading edge,” Lin says. He had helped build a variety of silicon technologies at Global Foundries and IBM, including the 14-nanometer SOI FinFET process that underpinned IBM’s Summit , which debuted in 2018 as the world’s top supercomputer. When he joined Intel that same year, he earned a fascinating assignment: leading the pathfinding device group to build Intel’s next-generation transistor, a gate-all-around design later dubbed RibbonFET. More: All News from Intel Foundry Direct Connect 2025 In 2011, Intel pioneered FinFET, the first major redesign of the CMOS transistor since its 1960s introduction. By the time Lin joined Intel, it was clear another new design would eventually be needed to keep making transistors smaller, faster and more efficient. If Lin wanted leading edge, he got it. Developing a new transistor would be arguably the most leading-edge job on the planet. The Intersection of Theory, Silicon Reality and Customer Needs Almost seven years later, Lin and his colleagues’ toil to turn RibbonFET from concept to high-volume manufacturing has been realized. RibbonFET makes its debut as part of the Intel 18A process node . Much anticipated for the past four years, Intel 18A is predicted to push Intel back to competitive leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing. It’s the manifestation of Intel’s redoubling on manufacturing prowess and its first major offering as a provider of foundry services for both internal and external chip design teams. And Lin has played a unique role in its development from his first day at Intel. Today, Lin is a senior principal engineer and leader of the Device Engineering Group within Intel Foundry Technology and Manufacturing – the division working on several future silicon process nodes, including Intel 18A, Intel 14A and beyond. Device engineering, it turns out, is where bet-the-company ambitions collide with the reality of what teams can reliably build on silicon wafers. Lin and his team lead a collaborative effort across Intel Foundry to set the performance targets for each future process node – for the transistors and interconnects – and then join forces to achieve those targets in silicon. They also encapsulate all the resulting specifications for each node in the process development kit, or PDK. “The PDK is how we talk to our customers,” explains Lin. The PDK is no less important than the silicon technologies it represents – he calls it an “implied contract” with customers for how the node will behave and perform. Owning all this puts device engineering at the center of process node development, reaching deep into both theory and physical silicon processes. “We are kind of a bridge, orchestrating all these things to build the PDK with the process and Design Technology Platform teams,” Lin says. It needs to digitally mirror the physical technologies as accurately as possible. To complicate things a bit, customers and partners need the PDK early, long before the silicon process is complete and ready for high-volume production. At the beginning, the PDK is the set of years-ahead projections the collective teams think they can achieve by the time process development is complete. Listening to Customers and Earning their Trust “We have to be humble,” Lin says. Foundry is all about customer service, “and we are learning to listen to customers and deliver what they need.” “Process development in leading-edge technology is exciting because there’s constant learning and improvement,” he notes. Customers expect some unpredictability on the silicon frontier, “but they want full transparency.” Embracing collaboration with partners fosters shared insights and, over time, builds trust between internal and external teams. Lin and team develop and maintain several PDKs in parallel – working to apply lessons across programs quickly and continuously improve the development process itself – but Intel 18A is special. “We’re trying to regain process leadership,” Lin says. Intel 18A contains a pair of new technologies that are radically different from their predecessors: PowerVia, which moves each chip’s power delivery network to the “back” (the bottom, in layman’s terms) side of the wafer, and RibbonFET, the totally new design for the transistors at the heart of every chip. Two years ago, Intel proved out PowerVia with a special in-between process node that used well-worn FinFET transistors as a control mechanism to iron out a new two-part manufacturing process, which goes from making chips like pizzas, from the bottom up, to making them like precision flipped omelets. RibbonFET uses a gate-all-around design and “is probably the most difficult transistor ever built,” Lin says. Continuing the geometric revolutions, RibbonFET flips the fins of the FinFET on their sides and stacks them vertically, where they can lie as “ribbons” much closer together (from around 30 nanometers apart to 10). It’s worth the trouble: With the gate surrounding the ribbons, the transistors work better. Altogether, each transistor switches faster (delivering more performance), runs more efficiently (using less power) and takes up less area on the wafer. It represents Moore’s Law fulfilled. What makes the RibbonFET hard to make is its three-dimensional intricacy. To peek into just one slice of it: Materials that form the suspended horizontal ribbons are layered across the entire bare silicon wafer first – and then etched away except where ribbons are needed. New layers are added, trenches are etched, and new materials are deposited in precise locations, sometimes atom by atom. Triple Trade-Offs, Fulfilling Projections and Unshakeable Optimism The whole process must be unfailingly repeatable and reliable. “Yield, performance and reliability always hurt each other because whenever you improve one, the other two might suffer,” Lin explains. “They always triple the trade-off.” But it can be defeated. Lin is a fan of the mindset cultivated by Youssef El-Mansy, a former Intel vice president who led the development of a dozen silicon processes until his retirement in 2004. The recipe, in short: set big goals (like regaining the process lead), take smart risks (see PowerVia’s development), and foster relentless and disciplined execution (hit the schedule). As development progresses, PDK changes are minimized and the silicon process is refined to match the commitments defined by the PDK. And a lot goes right: “The most fun part is when you see the silicon data meeting your projection,” Lin says. Last August, Intel Foundry announced that the 1.0 version of the Intel 18A PDK was released, but Lin and team were not done. Even though the Intel 18A process is entering risk production, Intel Foundry teams continue to improve and expand on its performance and capabilities. For Lin, the ultimate satisfaction arrives when the technologies reach their destination – in your next laptop or a world-beating supercomputer. “I just want to build something concrete that can help human life,” Lin says. He knows the next process node, and the next set of challenges, is always right around the corner. For this job, “You need to be a positive thinker and really feel patient about what you are doing,” he says. “You need to be pumped up for many, many years.” About Chung-Hsun Lin: Builder in Brief Home site: Hillsboro, Oregon Title: Senior principal engineer and area manager Team: Device Engineering Group, Logic Technology Development Years at Intel: 6 Management philosophy: “The only way to keep talent is to care about their career growth, define clear engineering goals and empower them to change the world with the resources to do it.” Favorite weekend getaway: Roasting coffee, sipping wine or tea Go-to exercise or entertainment for relaxation: Practicing euphonium and jogging Most-played music on the playlist: Gustav Mahler’s symphonies, conducted by Leonard Bernstein Intel Foundry Manufacturing Behind the Builders Related Posts Intel Foundry Intel Completes RAMP-C Program, Accelerating Momentum for Secure Enclave Program enabled validated prototypes, ecosystem readiness, and early customer engagement, creating a path to domestic leadership in high-volume manufacturing July 28, 2026 New Technologies Intel and Lens Technology Collaborate to Enable Advanced Semiconductor Packaging for the AI Era Collaboration combines Intel's advanced packaging expertise with Lens Technology's precision glass processing capabilities to deliver enhanced performance for future AI and datacenter workloads July 24, 2026 Intel Foundry Intel Invests €5 Billion to Expand Manufacturing in Europe Investment is expected to create permanent high-tech jobs and engage specialised tradespeople, while expanding leading-edge manufacturing capacity in Ireland. title: Resilience and Complexity: Amazing Bodily Changes During Pregnancy
summary: The blog article 'Resilience and Complexity: Amazing Bodily Changes During Pregnancy' explores the incredible transformations a woman's body undergoes during pregnancy. It delves into the complex ways the body adapts, showcasing resilience in supporting the growth and development of new life. From hormonal shifts to physical alterations, the article highlights key changes such as increased blood volume, the stretching of ligaments, and the adaptation of organs to make room for the growing fetus. It also touches on the emotional and psychological changes women experience. This article aims to give readers a deeper appreciation for the body's amazing ability to endure and thrive during this life-altering process.
body_text: Resilience and Complexity: Amazing Bodily Changes During Pregnancy Pregnancy is a remarkable journey that showcases the body's incredible ability to adapt and support new life. During this period, a woman's body undergoes a myriad of changes, both visible and invisible, to accommodate the growing fetus. These transformations are not just physical but also emotional and psychological, highlighting the resilience and complexity of the human body. Hormonal Shifts One of the first changes a pregnant woman experiences is a surge in hormones. Hormones such as estrogen and progesterone increase significantly, playing vital roles in maintaining the pregnancy and preparing the body for childbirth and breastfeeding. Estrogen helps in the development of the fetus and stimulates the growth of the uterus and improves blood flow, while progesterone relaxes the uterine muscles and helps prepare the breasts for milk production. Increased Blood Volume Another significant change is the increase in blood volume. By the time a woman reaches the end of her pregnancy, her blood volume has increased by about 50%. This increase is crucial for meeting the metabolic demands of the fetus and for ensuring that both the mother and baby receive sufficient nutrients and oxygen. Additionally, this change helps prepare the body for the blood loss that occurs during childbirth. Physical Alterations As the baby grows, the body undergoes various physical changes. The uterus expands, and the ligaments stretch to accommodate the growing fetus. Many women experience changes in their posture and balance due to the shift in their center of gravity. The skin also stretches, which can lead to stretch marks, and some women notice changes in their hair and nails. Organ Adaptation To make room for the growing baby, the organs in a woman's body must adjust. The stomach and intestines are pushed upward, while the diaphragm moves up to accommodate the expanding uterus. This can lead to changes in digestion and breathing patterns. The kidneys also work harder to filter increased waste products from the mother and the baby. Emotional and Psychological Changes Pregnancy is not just a physical transformation but also an emotional and psychological one. Hormonal fluctuations can lead to mood swings, and many women experience heightened emotions. It's normal for expectant mothers to feel a mix of excitement, anxiety, and even fear as they prepare for the arrival of their baby. Support from family, friends, and healthcare providers is crucial in helping women navigate these emotional changes. Appreciating the Body's Resilience The changes that occur during pregnancy highlight the body's resilience and adaptability. Despite the challenges, the human body is equipped to support the growth and development of new life. Understanding these changes can help expectant mothers appreciate the incredible work their bodies are doing and prepare them for the journey ahead. In conclusion, pregnancy is a testament to the body's ability to endure and thrive. From hormonal shifts to physical and emotional adaptations, each change serves a purpose in nurturing and protecting both the mother and her developing baby. By recognizing and understanding these transformations, we can gain a deeper appreciation for the amazing process that pregnancy truly is.

title: Certificação ESG: o que é e como funciona?
summary: Descubra o que é certificação ESG, a importância para o seu negócio, e o que uma empresa precisa para ter para obter esse selo.
body_text: A certificação ESG é um selo que comprova que as operações de uma empresa têm como base critérios de responsabilidade ambiental, social e de governança. Significa, portanto, que as atividades corporativas focam também a proteção do meio ambiente, da sociedade e a transparência. Essa é uma das certificações empresariais que mostra a idoneidade de um negócio, que comprova que o objetivo da companhia não é apenas obter lucro, mas também contribuir para um mundo melhor para todos, com respeito à natureza, à vida humana e à honestidade operacional. Além de melhorar a reputação da marca, empresas que trabalham dessa forma atraem mais público, reduzem riscos e custos relacionados a esses problemas. Neste artigo, você descobre o que é a certificação ESG, como funciona, a importância para o seu negócio, o impacto na rede de abastecimento e o que é preciso para obter esse selo. O que é certificação ESG? A certificação ESG é um documento que atesta que uma empresa segue padrões de reconhecimento nacional e, por vezes, internacional, de responsabilidade ambiental, social e de governança corporativa. Mostra ainda seu comprometimento com a vida humana, animal, fauna, flora e transparência operacional. Ter um selo ESG é vantajoso por diversos motivos. Um dos principais é que ajuda a atrair consumidores e aumentar as vendas. Uma pesquisa da Descarbonizar Soluções , empresa de soluções energéticas, revelou que 70% dos entrevistados afirmaram que o comprometimento ambiental da marca é um dos critérios que consideram no momento da compra . Desse grupo, 40% destacaram a responsabilidade ambiental como um fator determinante na tomada de decisão sobre a aquisição de um produto . Além de ir ao encontro do que os consumidores esperam atualmente das empresas, ter uma certificação ESG é benéfico, pois: reduz riscos ambientais, sociais e de governança e os gastos e transtornos relacionados ao tratamento dessas ameaças; aumenta a eficiência operacional e ajuda a evitar desperdícios; torna o negócio mais competitivo; promove a fidelização de clientes conscientes; garante alinhamento com as exigências regulatórias; fortalece a governança corporativa . Entenda mais sobre esse último tópico no artigo: “ Entenda a importância da governança ESG para a sua empresa ” Como funcionam os selos ESG? Os selos ESG funcionam como um documento que reconhece que uma empresa é comprometida com boas práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança em todas as suas frentes. Instituições independentes — como a ABNT, que emite o Rótulo Ecológico , e o Procel, Programa Nacional de Conservação de Energia Elétrica — avaliam dados, políticas e resultados da organização. Quando atende aos critérios, recebe o selo ESG como prova de sua conformidade e responsabilidade. A partir da emissão, os gestores podem usar a certificação ESG em relatórios, campanhas e materiais institucionais e, assim, reforçam a credibilidade perante investidores, consumidores e parceiros comerciais. Sugestão de leitura: “ Relatório ESG: o que é, qual a importância e como elaborar? ” O que uma empresa precisa para obter a certificação ESG? Saber o que uma empresa precisa para obter a certificação ESG é o primeiro passo para conquistar esse importante selo. O passo a passo tende a variar conforme o tipo de certificado e o órgão emissor. Porém, em linhas gerais, inclui: diagnóstico inicial; definição de metas ESG; implementação de práticas sustentáveis e éticas; monitoramento e registro de resultados; contratação de uma certificadora reconhecida; obtenção e divulgação do selo ESG; revisões periódicas e melhoria contínua. Entenda cada etapa em detalhes. 1. Diagnóstico inicial Os gestores devem iniciar a busca pela certificação ESG com o reconhecimento da realidade da empresa. Portanto, nesta etapa devem levantar e avaliar as práticas que já implementaram, a fim de identificar falhas e oportunidades de melhoria. Um diagnóstico executado corretamente é essencial para seguir para os próximos passos, pois evita decisões baseadas em achismos. 2. Definição de metas ESG A partir da análise anterior, os gestores e responsáveis por essa atividade devem estabelecer metas claras, mensuráveis e alinhadas aos critérios ESG , como emissão de gases de efeito estufa, grau de transparência em relatórios financeiros e percentual de diversidade no quadro de funcionários. As metas guiam o planejamento corporativo e mostram o compromisso da companhia com a evolução contínua. 3. Implementação de práticas sustentáveis e éticas Nesta fase, deve-se implementar práticas que ajudem a alcançar as metas. Pode envolver desde ajustes na cadeia de fornecimento até políticas de inclusão, programas de bem-estar, mudanças no consumo de recursos e fortalecimento da governança. Cada mudança precisa gerar impacto real e ser devidamente documentada. 4. Monitoramento e registro de resultados É crucial acompanhar e registrar todos os dados com precisão. A mensuração de resultados permite avaliar se as ações estão no caminho certo e corrigir o que ainda não está adequado. Além disso, promove a rastreabilidade e a transparência, dois dos critérios que as certificadoras exigem. 5. Contratação de uma certificadora reconhecida Nesta etapa, os responsáveis pela obtenção do selo ESG devem buscar uma instituição especializada, com credibilidade no mercado, para avaliar sua conformidade com os padrões socioambientais e de governança. Essa entidade realizará auditorias, entrevistas, análise documental e visitas técnicas, para garantir a concessão da certificação apenas às companhias que atenderam a todos os critérios. 6. Obtenção e divulgação do selo ESG Após a validação, a empresa recebe a certificação ESG e pode usá-la como selo oficial em suas comunicações. Esse reconhecimento aumenta a confiança do mercado e reforça a imagem da marca quanto à sua responsabilidade e compromisso com a sustentabilidade. 7. Revisões periódicas e melhoria contínua O selo ESG não é definitivo. Para renová-lo, é fundamental manter os padrões e submeter as atividades corporativas a revisões periódicas. Essa verificação reforça o comprometimento da companhia com boas práticas socioambientais e de governança em longo prazo e mantém a relevância de suas ações. Não deixe de ler este artigo: “ Certificações ambientais de fornecedores: por que e como verificar? ” A importância da sustentabilidade e certificações empresariais A sustentabilidade e as certificações empresariais são importantes porque mostram que o negócio vai além do lucro e age com responsabilidade em todas as suas frentes. O selo ESG, por exemplo, fortalece a reputação, atrai investidores e consumidores que valorizam marcas alinhadas a causas socioambientais. Contudo, não se resume a um diferencial para destacar a marca no mercado, mas, sim, a um compromisso com o futuro das pessoas e do meio ambiente. Porém, não basta a empresa se comprometer com critérios ESG e obter selos relacionados. Todos os que participam de suas atividades precisam seguir o mesmo caminho e ter o mesmo nível de comprometimento.
